1940-1945_late_colonial_food_order.label: Late colonial food-order regime
1940-1945_late_colonial_food_order.interpretation: Taiwan-side local food practices exist within late Japanese colonial food, market, and wartime scarcity conditions; lu rou fan terminology must be mined from newspapers, cookbooks, and market records rather than assumed.

1946-1949_postwar_transition.label: Postwar transition regime
1946-1949_postwar_transition.interpretation: Taiwan's food system is reorganized after Japanese colonial rule and KMT takeover; local Taiwanese foods remain socially marked against elite Chinese regional cuisines.

1950-1978_taiwan_side_popular_food.label: Taiwan-side popular-food and stall-to-shop regime
1950-1978_taiwan_side_popular_food.interpretation: Lu rou fan develops mainly within Taiwan-side street-stall, market, and popular-food discourse, while mainland public-commercial circulation remains structurally limited.

1979-1987_brand_formalization_and_reopen.label: Brand formalization and latent-contact regime
1979-1987_brand_formalization_and_reopen.interpretation: Taiwan-side lu rou fan vendors begin formalizing into branches and brands, while mainland economic opening creates background conditions but not yet large-scale direct cross-strait food commerce.

1988-2001_cross_strait_mobility.label: Cross-strait mobility and Taiwanese-food recognition regime
1988-2001_cross_strait_mobility.interpretation: Cross-strait travel, investment, and media contact make Taiwan food more legible, but lu rou fan is not yet a dominant mainland platform commodity.

2002-2013_taiwan_capital_gateway.label: Taiwan-capital casual-dining gateway regime
2002-2013_taiwan_capital_gateway.interpretation: Taiwanese restaurant chains enter mainland cities through Shanghai/YRD and major urban commercial districts. Taiwaneseness is framed as leisure dining, chain management, and broad Taiwanese cuisine.

2014-2020_hk_taiwan_authenticity.label: Hong Kong/Taiwan authenticity and night-market regime
2014-2020_hk_taiwan_authenticity.interpretation: Hong Kong or Taiwan-linked brands stage Taiwaneseness through founder/chef origin stories, night-market food, and authenticity claims.

2021-2023_mainland_platform_transition.label: Mainland Taiwan-themed platform transition regime
2021-2023_mainland_platform_transition.interpretation: Mainland-origin Taiwan-themed brands and platform-visible small-store formats narrow Taiwanese cuisine into rice bowls, snacks, and chainable lunch formats.

2024-2025_lu_rou_fan_wanghong_boom.label: Lu rou fan wanghong and value-platform boom regime
2024-2025_lu_rou_fan_wanghong_boom.interpretation: Taiwanese lu rou fan becomes a specialized rice-bowl category shaped by price/value discourse, mall expansion, platform visibility, Michelin/award authority, prepared-food standardization tensions, and consumer-downgrade narratives.

2026_retrospective_context_only.label: Retrospective context only
2026_retrospective_context_only.interpretation: Use 2026 sources only when they retrospectively document developments through 2025 or when clearly marked as outside the main analytical window.
